posts.author: Glenn
posts.content_md:
Anybody ever take a pic of your point-source HOE in action (using your reference laser line as the illuminating object, of course), showing it magnify something your laser line is shining on?

Do you have a picture of this HOE you can post?

Except for a diffraction grating, does anyone have any pic of any HOE in action?

It seems to make sense that the grating spacing of a transmission hologram is the same as the wavelength of the reference beam used to make the hologram. Is this true?

On a different note, has anyone ever tried this:

[http://corticalcafe.com/prog_CGHmaker.htm](http://corticalcafe.com/prog_CGHmaker.htm)

and get it to actually work? Even w/my 1,200 dpi laserjet, I can't seem to get a viable HOE out of it, even though the author of the code swears by it. One such HOE looks like this, and he calls it an Fresnel Zone Plate:

![Image](http://corticalcafe.com/Images/fresnelZone_realBin.gif)

He says this HOE will act exactly as a traditional magnifying lens would, provided coherent light is used (and this also ties into the question I asked, above).

Here's another, similar image, intended to be printed on a transparency:

![Image](http://tbn0.google.com/images?q=tbn:K8_kuVLhPw2jmM:http://corticalcafe.com/Images/Holo_letterA_4m_RealBin2.gif)
